scenes.title: 1974 North Vancouver: 230-Foot Swaying Capilano Canyon Bridge (50% Phone Calls!) vs Solid 10-Foot Cedar Bridge (12.5%)
scenes.era: 1974, Capilano Canyon, North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

layout.description: Sunlit high-key Pacific Northwest cedar-forest gorge spanning the iconic **450-foot-long, 5-foot-wide swaying wooden-plank and wire-cable Capilano Suspension Bridge** high above rushing canyon water, paired in clear documentary split comparison with the **sturdy low 10-foot cedar bridge** upstream and a crisp **Post-Bridge Callback Board ('Low Solid Bridge: 12.5% Called | 230-Ft Swaying Bridge: 50.0% Called — 4x!')**.

positions.who: Female UBC Interviewer mannequin ('Gloria', in 1974 denim-and-knit Pacific Northwest jacket holding a clipboard and tear-off phone number slip)
positions.where: standing mid-span on the swaying wooden planks handing the tear-off study contact slip to a male crosser

positions.who: Male Bridge Crosser mannequin (in 1974 windbreaker and jeans, one hand steadying on the wire cable handrail)
positions.where: feeling his heart pound over the 230-foot drop while smiling intently as he pockets the tear-off phone number slip!

props.name: swaying wooden-plank & steel-cable suspension bridge vs low solid cedar bridge comparison
props.period_detail: embodies high vs low sympathetic arousal visually in one glance

props.name: clipboard with TAT picture card + perforated tear-off phone number corner ('50% vs 12.5%')
props.period_detail: the exact behavioral dependent measure from JPSP 1974

actions.verb_sequence: steps onto the swaying 230-foot bridge gripping the cable as his chest pounds -> Female Interviewer shows TAT card and hands over the tear-off phone slip -> Crosser misreads canyon adrenaline as chemistry and dials her number at 4x the low-bridge rate!

reactions.reaction: grins convinced he just felt 'love at first sight' mid-canyon

reactions.who: Dutton & Aron mannequins (at trailhead with Study 2 park-bench timer)
reactions.reaction: log calls dropping from 65% on-bridge to 30% once pulses cool 10 minutes later

scenes.wardrobe: 1974 Canadian outdoor casual attire: nylon hiking windbreaker, plaid flannel overshirt, knit sweater, and denim.
scenes.lighting: Crisp high-key Pacific Northwest forest-canyon daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Meet the exact same interviewer on a sturdy 10-foot creek bridge and 12.5% of men call — meet her 230 feet up a swaying canyon suspension bridge and 50% dial her number!

key_visual.description: a sunlit Pacific Northwest forest canyon suspension bridge high above rapids where a clipboard interviewer hands a tear-off phone slip to a male crosser gripping the wire rail beside a 50%-vs-12.5% callback chart

scenes.title: Study 2 Proof: Waiting 10 Minutes on a Park Bench Halves the Spark!
scenes.era: 1974, Capilano Park cedar bench past the bridge exit

layout.description: Calm sunlit park bench 10 minutes past the suspension bridge exit with resting heart-rate comparison.

positions.where: talking calmly once heart rate returns to normal — callback rate drops from 65% (on bridge) to 30% (on bench)!

props.name: On-Bridge (65%) vs 10-Min Cooled Bench (30%) placard
props.period_detail: proves thrill-seeker personality did NOT explain the effect

actions.verb_sequence: sits 10 minutes calming pulse -> meets interviewer -> half the misattribution vanishes

scenes.recognition_hook: Same thrill-seekers, same scary bridge — simply waiting ten minutes on a park bench for their hearts to slow down cut phone calls in half!

actions.verb_sequence: traces amygdala-insula arousal up to prefrontal attribution

scenes.recognition_hook: Adrenaline isn't a blind love potion — it's an emotional volume knob that makes charming people magnetic and annoying people intolerable!
